# Quality control: Levey–Jennings and Westgard rules — math appendix

<!-- GENERATED by video_studio/scripts/docs.mjs (same code as the video: video_studio/src/lib/qc.js) -->

**Illustrative control data — invented for teaching; not a real control material, lot or method.** Two levels: L1 "Low" lot DEMO-1, target mean 5, SD 0.2; L2 "High" lot DEMO-2, target mean 15, SD 0.5 (entered in the app as "Our laboratory's data"). Runs are designed by z-score; the value is mean + z·SD.

## 1. Rules (as implemented by the app, `lib/features/qc/qc_rules.dart`; Westgard JO et al., Clin Chem 1981;27:493–501; app decisions D-20, D-27)

- z = (x − mean) / SD; a value exactly at ±k SD is not a violation.
- 1-2s: one value beyond ±2 SD — **warning** (inspect with the other rules); all other rules reject.
- 1-3s: one value beyond ±3 SD. 2-2s: two consecutive beyond 2 SD on the same side (within a run across levels, or one level in two consecutive runs). R-4s: within one run one value above +2 SD and another below −2 SD. 4-1s: four consecutive beyond 1 SD on one side; 10x: ten consecutive on one side of the mean (within one level, or across levels).
- A rejected run's values are not used by later rules or in the observed statistics (D-27).

## 6. What the numbers do NOT mean

- No control material, lot, analyte target or acceptance limit is implied; mmol/L is only the unit field of the demo test.
- Westgard rules are shown as the app implements them (all rejection rules checked on every run, 1-2s as a warning — stricter than the classic 1-2s "gate", explained in D-20). Which rules a laboratory uses is set by its QC procedure.
- "Find the cause" is the general action after a rejection; the app's guide "What to do when QC is rejected" lists the steps.
